episodes.title: What sautéing does to your veggies

youtube.title: What sautéing really does to your veggies #Shorts
youtube.description:
Oil helps your body absorb some nutrients in carrots, spinach and broccoli. Heat can lower the vitamin C in peppers and tomatoes. So sautéing is a trade, not good or bad. Food education, not diet advice.

#PanTheory #CookingScience #FoodScience #Shorts

episodes.title: Why onions make you cry, and the droplets you can't see

youtube.title: Why onions make you cry, and the droplets you can't see #Shorts
youtube.description:
A lab study filmed an onion being cut and saw tiny droplets burst out at up to about 90 mph. A reaction in the cut onion makes an eye irritant that sets off tears. A sharper blade threw fewer, slower droplets, but this is one study in one lab that tracked droplets, not tears.

#PanTheory #CookingScience #Onions #Shorts

tiktok.title: Your onion shoots tiny droplets when you cut it. A sharper blade threw fewer droplets in one lab

instagram.caption:

episodes.title: Your towel grows a film of bacteria. Does it hurt your skin?

youtube.title: Your towel grows a film of bacteria. Does it hurt your skin? #Shorts
youtube.description:
A 6-month study of towels in 26 households found a film of bacteria builds up with normal use. That study didn't look at anyone's skin or test disposable towels, so whether it harms skin is unproven: receipt total UNKNOWN. Dermatologists do say don't share towels. Education, not medical advice.

#SkinReceipts #Skincare #SkinScience #Shorts

episodes.title: Does drinking water hydrate your skin? 49 women tested it

youtube.title: Does drinking water hydrate your skin? 49 women tested it #Shorts
youtube.description:
In one small study, 49 women added about 2 liters of water a day for 4 weeks and skin hydration readings rose, mostly in people who took in less water to begin with. There was no comparison group, and a 2018 review called the evidence weak, so the receipt total is UNKNOWN. Education, not medical advice.

episodes.title: Your head is older than your feet

youtube.title: Your head is older than your feet
youtube.description:
Your head ticks a tiny bit faster than your feet. Gravity slows time, so the higher you are, the faster your time runs.

In 2010, physicists at NIST, a U.S. lab, raised an atomic clock by about a foot (two steps up a staircase). The higher clock ticked faster. Over a 79-year life, that adds up to about 90 billionths of a second. GPS satellite clocks run fast too, so engineers set them slower before launch.

Case file 001: TRUE. The higher you are, the faster your time runs.

Source: NIST news release, 23 Sept 2010.

#Shorts #Science #Physics #Relativity #UnrealActually

tiktok.title: Your head is older than your feet

instagram.caption:
Unreal, Actually · Ep 1

Your head is older than your feet. Gravity slows time, so the higher you are, the faster your time runs. In 2010, NIST raised an atomic clock by about a foot, and it ticked faster. Over a lifetime, about 90 billionths of a second. Far too small to feel, but real.

episodes.title: What happens if you fall into a black hole

youtube.title: What happens if you fall into a black hole #Shorts
youtube.description:
Fall toward a black hole and watchers far away would see you slow down and freeze. NASA's simulation says the fall takes about three hours on your own clock, then seconds to spaghettification. Nobody has watched anyone fall in, so the case file reads UNPROVEN.

#BlackHole #Space #Science #Shorts

tiktok.title: To anyone far away, you'd freeze at the edge of a black hole

instagram.caption:
Unreal, Actually · Ep 2
Fall into a black hole and to anyone far away you'd seem to freeze at the edge. NASA's simulation shows what it would be like for you. Case file 002: UNPROVEN.
